FILMMAKING NOTES / VANSH RASTOGI

Character Continuity in AI Films

A connected film begins with consistent decisions.

Create a reference set that answers real shot questions

One portrait may describe a face but not how the character looks in profile, in a wide shot or under different light. Build a compact set of clear reference views where the project needs them. Keep facial proportions, age, hairstyle and distinguishing features consistent across those views. Conflicting references can make later shot choices harder to evaluate.

Write down the details that must not change

Separate identity from styling. A character record can include the face reference, hairstyle, facial hair, wardrobe, shoes and recurring accessories. For a sequence, also record props and which hand holds them. These notes are especially useful when production is split across short clips. A detail that looks minor in isolation can become distracting at the cut between two shots.

Plan the action and screen direction

Describe where the character starts, which direction they face, what they do and where the shot ends. Track entrances, exits and the direction of a look. A walking scene can feel disconnected if the next clip reverses the travel direction without a clear reason. Establishing the action in the shot plan reduces the amount that later editing must repair.

Keep lighting and environment relationships believable

Continuity is more than a matching face. The time of day, light direction, background layout and distance between characters help the viewer understand the space. For connected shots, retain a small environment reference and note the key light sources. Close-ups can vary in composition while still sharing a believable color temperature and shadow direction.

Review boundaries between clips

Inspect both the shot itself and its join with the next shot. Compare the last useful frame of one clip with the opening of the next. Watch for wardrobe changes, shifting props, inconsistent eyelines and sudden changes in body position. A clean transition may use a reaction, an insert or a wider view, but the choice should serve the story rather than simply hide every mismatch.

Finish for clarity, not just resolution

Upscaling can change presentation size, but it cannot reliably recover detail that was never present. Check identity, movement and texture before spending time on a higher-resolution finish. The edit, sound and color should support the same emotional beat across the sequence. Final review on both a large display and a small mobile screen can reveal different continuity and readability problems.
